'''Konrad Walter Gams''' (9 August 1934 – 9 April 2017) was an Austrian [[mycologist]]. He worked as a scientist for his entire career at the Centraalbureau voor Schimmelcultures ([[Westerdijk Fungal Biodiversity Institute]]) in the Netherlands.<ref name="westerdijkinstitute.nl-2017">{{Cite web |date=2017-05-10 |title=Dr Walter Gams passed away |url=http://www.westerdijkinstitute.nl/BioloMICSNews.aspx?Rec=10451 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180822181541/http://www.westerdijkinstitute.nl/BioloMICSNews.aspx?Rec=10451 |archive-date=2018-08-22 |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=westerdijkinstitute.nl}}</ref> He served in the international authority on classification of fungi, the Special Committee on Fungi and Lichens (renamed Nomenclatural Committee for Fungi), from which he contributed to the development of the ''[[International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi and plants]]''.<ref name="Seifert-2019">{{Cite journal |last1=Seifert |first1=Keith A. |last2=Zare |first2=Rasoul |last3=Summerbell |first3=Richard C. |date=2019-07-04 |title=In memoriam: Walter Gams (1934–2017) |journal=Mycologia |volume=111 |issue=4 |pages=690–697 |doi=10.1080/00275514.2019.1619058 |issn=0027-5514 |pmid=31194652 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Some species of fungi he identified became sources of pharmaceutical drugs such as [[cephalosporin C]] ([[antibiotic]]) from ''[[Sarocladium strictum]]'' and ''Acremonium chrysogenum'',<ref name="Tian-2017">{{Cite journal |last1=Tian |first1=Jin |last2=Lai |first2=Daowan |last3=Zhou |first3=Ligang |date=2017-05-01 |title=Secondary Metabolites from Acremonium Fungi: Diverse Structures and Bioactivities |url=https://www.ingentaconnect.com/content/ben/mrmc/2017/00000017/00000007/art00005 |journal=Mini-Reviews in Medicinal Chemistry |volume=17 |issue=7 |pages=603–632 |doi=10.2174/1389557516666160914194134 |pmid=27633747 }}</ref> and [[ciclosporin]] ([[immunosuppressant]]) from ''[[Tolypocladium inflatum]].''<ref name="von Wartburg-1988">{{Citation |last1=von Wartburg |first1=Albert |title=1 Cyclosporins, Fungal Metabolites with Immunosuppressive Activities |date=1988-01-01 |volume=25 |pages=1–33 |editor-last=Ellis |editor-first=G. P. |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0079646808702765 |access-date=2025-07-18 |publisher=Elsevier |last2=Traber |first2=René |series=Progress in Medicinal Chemistry |doi=10.1016/S0079-6468(08)70276-5 |pmid=3076967 |isbn=978-0-444-80965-0 |editor2-last=West |editor2-first=G. B.|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Gams was born in [[Zurich]], Switzerland, to [[Helmut Gams]] and Margarete Gams-Schima. His father, originally from [[Brünn]] (now Brno in the Czech Republic), was a botanist and a professor at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]], Germany, and then at the [[University of Innsbruck]], Austria.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Pitschmann H |year=1977 |title=Nachruf auf em. o. Univ.-Prof. Dr. phil. Helmut Gams (1893-1976) |url=http://www.zobodat.at/pdf/BERI_64_0207-0222.pdf |journal=Berichte des Naturwissenschaftlich Medizinischen Vereins in Innsbruck |language=de |volume=64 |pages=207–222}}</ref> He studied botany in his father's department for his bacherlor's degree. He went to the [[University of Zurich]] to study under his uncle Emil Schmid for his master's degree. He returned to Innsbruck and obtained a PhD in 1960. With a post-doctoral scholarship, he went to UK to work with Dennis Parkinson, a microbiologist at the [[University of Liverpool]].<ref name="Seifert-2019" />

In 1961, Gams was recruited as a research associate by Klaus Heinz Domsch at the research institute, Biologischen Bundesanstalt für Land-und Forstwirtschaft (Federal Biological Research Centre for Agriculture and Forestry) in Kiel-Kitzeberg, Germany.<ref name="Seifert-2019" /> His works with Domsch on fungal diversity was documented in several books and research articles,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gams |first1=W. |last2=Domsch |first2=K. H. |date=1967-06-01 |title=Beiträge zur Anwendung der Bodenwaschtechnik für die Isolierung von Bodenpilzen |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00406674 |journal=Archiv für Mikrobiologie|volume=58 |issue=2 |pages=134–144 |doi=10.1007/BF00406674 |bibcode=1967ArMic..58..134G |issn=1432-072X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Domsch |first1=K. H. |last2=Gams |first2=W. |last3=Weber |first3=E. |date=1968 |title=Der Einfluß verschiedener Vorfrüchte auf das Bodenpilzspektrum in Weizenfeldern |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/jpln.19681190206 |journal=Zeitschrift für Pflanzenernährung und Bodenkunde|volume=119 |issue=2 |pages=134–149 |doi=10.1002/jpln.19681190206 |bibcode=1968ZPflD.119..134D |issn=1522-2624|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Domsch |first1=K. H. |last2=Gams |first2=W. |date=1969-04-01 |title=Variability and potential of a soil fungus population to decompose pectin, xylan and carboxymethyl-cellulose |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0038-0717%2869%2990031-5 |journal=Soil Biology and Biochemistry |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=29–36 |doi=10.1016/0038-0717(69)90031-5 |bibcode=1969SBiBi...1...29D |issn=0038-0717|url-access=subscription }}</ref> including two monumental monographs, ''Fungi in Agricultural Soils'' (1971, original in German in 1970<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Klein |first=Deana T. |date=1974 |title=Fungi in Agricultural Soils. K. H. Domsch , W. Gams , P. S. Hudson |url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/407955 |journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology |volume=49 |issue=1 |pages=74–75 |doi=10.1086/407955 |issn=0033-5770|url-access=subscription }}</ref>) and ''Compendium of Soil Fungi'' (in two volumes, first published in 1980).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Seifert |first=K. A. |date=2008 |title=Compendium of Soil Fungi - by K.H. Domsch, W. Gams & T.-H. Anderson |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1365-2389.2008.01052_1.x |journal=European Journal of Soil Science|volume=59 |issue=5 |pages=1007 |doi=10.1111/j.1365-2389.2008.01052_1.x |bibcode=2008EuJSS..59.1007S |issn=1365-2389|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Together they discovered novel fungal species such as ''Paraphaeosphaeria sporulosa''<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Giraldo |first1=A. |last2=Crous |first2=P. W. |date=2019-03-01 |title=Inside Plectosphaerellaceae |journal=Studies in Mycology |volume=92 |pages=227–286 |doi=10.1016/j.simyco.2018.10.005 |pmid=30518989 |issn=0166-0616|pmc=6276054 }}</ref> and ''Podila'' (''Mortierella'') ''epigama''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Vandepol |first1=Natalie |last2=Liber |first2=Julian |last3=Desirò |first3=Alessandro |last4=Na |first4=Hyunsoo |last5=Kennedy |first5=Megan |last6=Barry |first6=Kerrie |last7=Grigoriev |first7=Igor V. |last8=Miller |first8=Andrew N. |last9=O’Donnell |first9=Kerry |last10=Stajich |first10=Jason E. |last11=Bonito |first11=Gregory |display-authors=8 |date=2020 |title=Resolving the Mortierellaceae phylogeny through synthesis of multi-gene phylogenetics and phylogenomics |journal=Fungal Diversity|volume=104 |issue=1 |pages=267–289 |doi=10.1007/s13225-020-00455-5 |pmid=33364917 |issn=1560-2745 |pmc=7751987}}</ref> Gams left Biologischen Bundesanstalt to join the Centraalbureau voor Schimmelcultures at Baarn (renamed as [[Westerdijk Fungal Biodiversity Institute]] and relocated at Utrecht) in the Netherlands. He worked there until his retirement in 1999.<ref name="Stadler-2019">{{Cite journal |last1=Stadler |first1=Marc |last2=Schroers |first2=Hans-Josef |date=2019-02-01 |title=Editorial to the special issue in honor of Walter Gams |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s11557-018-1457-7 |journal=Mycological Progress|volume=18 |issue=1 |pages=1–4 |doi=10.1007/s11557-018-1457-7 |bibcode=2019MycPr..18....1S |issn=1861-8952}}</ref>

Since 1984,<ref name="Seifert-2019" /> Gams became a permanent member of the Nomenclature Committee for Fungi (a part of the [[International Botanical Congress]]<ref>{{Cite web |year=2018 |title=Nomenclature Committee for Fungi |url=http://www.ima-mycology.org/nomenclature/nomenclature-committee-fungi |access-date=2021-09-25 |website=International Mycological Association |archive-date=2021-09-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210925163854/http://www.ima-mycology.org/nomenclature/nomenclature-committee-fungi |url-status=dead }}</ref>) that maintains the ''International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi and plants.'' He served as the committee's secretary for several years.<ref name="Stadler-2019" /> He published over 300 publications, including six books, created one new order, 10 new families, 57 generic names, and 622 species epithets. Three genera and 39 species were named after him.<ref name="Seifert-2019" />

Among Gams's discoveries of fungal species, ''Acremonium chrysogenum'', ''Sarocladium strictum'', and ''Tolypocladium inflatum'' become important in pharmceutical science and industry as they are sources of clinical drugs. ''Acremonium chrysogenum'' and ''Sarocladium strictum'' produced cephalosporin C, one of the most widely used antibiotics, and which in turn is the source several related cephalosporins.<ref name="Tian-2017" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Liu |first1=Ling |last2=Chen |first2=Zhen |last3=Liu |first3=Wuyi |last4=Ke |first4=Xiang |last5=Tian |first5=Xiwei |last6=Chu |first6=Ju |date=2022-10-01 |title=Cephalosporin C biosynthesis and fermentation in Acremonium chrysogenum |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00253-022-12181-w |journal=Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology|volume=106 |issue=19 |pages=6413–6426 |doi=10.1007/s00253-022-12181-w |pmid=36114850 |issn=1432-0614|url-access=subscription }}</ref> ''Tolypocladium inflatum'' is the source of ciclosporin A,<ref name="von Wartburg-1988" /> which is used as immunosuppressant and is approved for use in [[atopic dermatitis]] in dogs and [[allergic dermatitis]] in cats.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Palmeiro |first=Brian S. |date=2013-01-01 |title=Cyclosporine in Veterinary Dermatology |url=https://www.vetsmall.theclinics.com/article/S0195-5616(12)00146-5/abstract |journal=Veterinary Clinics: Small Animal Practice|volume=43 |issue=1 |pages=153–171 |doi=10.1016/j.cvsm.2012.09.007 |issn=0195-5616 |pmid=23182330}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Gams never used his first name and even shunned it as his initial.<ref name="westerdijkinstitute.nl-2017" /> Although he spent most of his lifetime in the Netherlands, he remained an Austrian citizen throughout life.<ref name="Stadler-2019" /> In 1972, he married Sophia Aaltine Luinge with whom he had two daughters, Hedi (Hedwig) and Hilde (Mechthilde).<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2017 |title=In remembrance: [Konrad] Walter Gams (1934–2017) |journal=Mycotaxon |volume=132 |issue=2 |pages=xi–xii |doi=10.5248/132-2 |doi-access=free}}</ref> He and Sophia were passionate musicians, playing and composing several classical and folk music at different occasions.<ref name="Seifert-2019" />

Gams founded a charity programme called "Studienstiftung mykologische Systematik und Ökologie" in 1995 for educational funding of young mycologists, particularly from poor backgrounds.<ref name="Seifert-2019" /> The foundation is now administered by the [[Deutschsprachige Mykologische Gesellschaft]] (German Mycological Society).<ref name="Stadler-2019" />

== Awards and honours ==
* Honorary members of [[British Mycological Society]], Iranian Mycological Society, and [[Mycological Society of America]]<ref name="Seifert-2019" />
* Distinguished Mycologist Award of the Mycological Society of America (2005)<ref name="Seifert-2019" />
* Anton de Bary medal of the Deutschen Phytomedizinischen Gesellschaft (2012)<ref name="Seifert-2019" />
